findings.problem: Beat 1 ends with an orange ring and a green tick labelled 'keep' on the best candidate only (score 5), i.e. the EA keeps the best and drops the rest. That is the 'only the best' strong selection that scene 6 (and boss question on the single best copied 50 times) teaches is a broken ingredient. Storyboard-vs-lesson disagreement; lesson 1.4 only says an EA needs a score.
findings.fix: Drop the 'keep' tick, or change it to 'fittest' / 'likelier to be picked' (no tick, no 'keep'), so scoring is shown as input to biased selection, not winner-takes-all.
findings.evidence: s9@4.5: bar 5 ringed with 'keep' tick; scene 6 s6@7 marks 'only the best' as a red cross.

findings.problem: Caption 'Change one letter at random. Better? Keep it.' contradicts the on-screen sticker 'not worse?' and the lesson rule (keep the change if it is not worse, i.e. ties are kept). A learner reads 'better' as strictly better.
findings.fix: Caption: 'Change one letter at random. Not worse? Keep it.' Same wording fix for the scene-5 caption 'One climber keeps steps only if better.' (the code and the app accept equal fitness, f(m) >= f(i)).
findings.evidence: s3@3 caption vs the 'not worse?' sticker; scene-05 caption at 1.9-4.2.

findings.problem: Caption 'The monkey is still on 6 of 28.' is inaccurate: 6/28 is the monkey's best-ever string (reached at try 47). Its current string at that moment scores about 1/28 (as the tiles show). The chip says 'best 6 / 28', the caption says 'on 6 of 28'.
findings.fix: Caption: 'The monkey's best is still 6 of 28.'
findings.evidence: s4@9.6: monkey tiles show one green E, chip 'best 6 / 28', caption 'still on 6 of 28'.

findings.problem: Caption 'Monkey: a 41-digit number of tries.' and the sticker 1.2 x 10^40 are the EXPECTED number of random tries (27^28, lesson: 'on average the monkey needs 27^28'), while the panel above shows the monkey after only 3,037 tries. Without the word 'expected' a learner could read it as the monkey's actual count in this race. Numbers themselves are right (27^28 = 11972515182562019788602740026717047105681, 41 digits; keeper 3,037 tries, 894 string changes; monkey best 6 at try 47; all re-computed independently).
findings.fix: Caption: 'Monkey needs about 1.2 x 10^40 tries on average. Keeper: 3,037.' or add 'on average'.

findings.problem: The chip 'average 49%' (to 95%) and the bar under it never say what the percentage is of. Lesson/app say 'of max' / '% of the best'. A first-time learner may read it as an accuracy or a probability.
findings.fix: Label 'average 49% of best' (or 'fitness 49% of the best'), keeping the bar.

findings.problem: Recombination is shown here as the midpoint of the two parents' positions on the landscape (that is what the lecture playground does), but scene 7 teaches recombination as cut-and-splice of genes (AAA + BBB). The two pictures of the same operator disagree, and the lesson step 1.3 only describes the splice.
findings.fix: Add a tiny hint in the Recombine ghost (e.g. caption 'Optional: blend two parents.') or note in scene 7 that on a landscape the blend sits between the parents. At minimum keep the caption wording 'mix two parents' without implying cutting.
findings.evidence: s8@6 purple arcs to a midpoint ring versus s7@11 AAABBB.

findings.problem: Headline 'One generation: select, vary, replace' lists three steps while the ribbon (and boss-quiz order the scene follows) has five: Score, Select, Recombine, Mutate, Replace. Score is the first step in the lesson's flow chart for the order question and is missing from the headline.
findings.fix: Headline 'One generation: score, select, vary, replace', or 'One generation, five steps'.

findings.problem: Caption/headline say 'Twenty climbers' and the lesson analogy is twenty independent hikers, but the shown algorithm is not independent hikers: dots copy the fitter of two random dots with +-4 noise (selection + mutation, the playground's 'weak' bias) while the single climber uses keep-if-better. So the scene credits the population alone for 42 -> 167 of 200 although selection also changes. This matches the app's playground (verified: 42 and 167 re-computed with mulberry32(1), same nextGen), but the 'Ingredient 1' framing is slightly generous.
findings.fix: Optional: caption 'Twenty climbers share what works and compete.' (or leave and accept, it matches the lesson).

findings.problem: The lecture's selling point from lesson 1.1 ('good results in reasonable time on messy real problems') is never shown or captioned; only the three systems and 'no one is in charge' are. Also the ant model (scent deposit divided by trail length, long trail = half scent per ant) is invented for the pictogram and not stated in the lesson, though it is the standard ACO idea and nothing numeric is displayed.
findings.fix: Optional: add the selling point to the final caption (e.g. 'No boss, good answers fast. Today: evolution.'). No change needed for the ant model.

findings.problem: Page title is duplicated: 'Lecture 1 · Lecture 1 · What is NIC? · CSLingo video' (lectures 5 and 6 read 'Lecture 5 · Encodings · CSLingo video').

Verification summary, no action needed: every quoted number re-computed independently from the lesson algorithms and matches the video: CAT/QZT tries and pips; weasel 28 characters, 27 choices, 27^28 (41 digits); keeper(17) 3,037 tries, 894 changes, milestones 8/183/507/904/1362/3037; monkey(117) best 6 (tries 3,3,31,47); multimodal landscape hills 30/74/120/167/209 (55/66/53/100/79% of best; the outline's 80% for hill 209 is really 79%, not shown on screen); climber(23) 16 candidates and hill 30 at generation 8; popRun(16) start positions and star-hill counts 2,2,2,2,4,4,2,1,2,2,4,5,6,7,12,19,20; test200 42/200 and 167/200; picks(46) sequence and counts 10/6/3/1 with chances 47.4/31.6/15.8/5.3 (rounded 47/32/16/5 sums to 100); popRun(40,6,5,rec) start 153,195,6,166,83,182 (51,28,16,100,50,51), generation 1 children (3,0,160,156)(1,0,174,177)(2,5,94,95)(3,3,166,163)(0,5,168,170)(3,0,160,161), pick counts 4,1,1,4,0,2, averages 49/73/82/92/93/95; scene 2 bar generations (means 57.7/74.5/88.0/96.7) and ant waves 5/5, 6/4, 7/3 giving scents 19/7 (widths 12.5/6.5); scene 9 scores 2/4/5 of 6.
